gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-ibm-plex-sans-tha: Bold, loud and a bit goofy, Happy Monkey leads with wide gaps in its e. IBM Plex Sans Thai Looped follows in a clean sans-serif, its curves left open and its line thinner and quieter than the heading's fixed nib.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-imprima: Distinctive from the first glance, Happy Monkey draws every line like it was cut with a ruler. Imprima takes over with a smooth, tube-like look and flared terminals, giving that display heading a friendlier plain sans to lean on.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-inclusive-sans: Inclusive Sans reads contemporary and businesslike, with round letters whose rims match the stems and curves left open at the ends. Happy Monkey then shouts over the top in its ruler-straight strokes, and the sans-serif underneath simply keeps talking.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-inria-sans: Happy Monkey's wide-open e is the thing you notice first, a gap you could post a letter through. Inria Sans does the quieter job, with tubular strokes like bent copper pipe and c openings you can see through, which suits a plain sans.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-istok-web: Istok Web reads modern and friendly, with rounded letters and a clearly open side. Happy Monkey brings bold, uniform strokes with no contrast between stems and joins, so the heading stands out while the plain sans below stays easy-going.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-jost: Jost reads clean and professional, with broad gaps at its terminals. Happy Monkey is best at grabbing attention with ruler-straight bold lines, while the sans does its best work in quietly keeping a unit-width stroke going.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-jura: Jura brings strokes as constant as bent wire, with s curves that open wide at both ends. Jura is a plain sans that would sit well beneath Happy Monkey's bold heading if the body text is given a modest size.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-k2d: Chunky, playful and loud. Happy Monkey's ruler-straight lines lead, then K2D follows in clean sans-serif, with tube-like strokes that hold thickness through every bend and terminals hanging well clear of the bowl, so paragraphs flow smoothly.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-kanchenjunga: Happy Monkey is the loud one here, bold and ruler-straight with wide gaps in its e. And Kanchenjunga, a sans-serif with the steady line of a technical drafting pen, holds its shapes open and sharp beneath it.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-kantumruy-pro: Approachable and easygoing, Kantumruy Pro is a sans with an e whose eye opens clearly to the right. Happy Monkey does bold, distinctive display best, while Kantumruy Pro does smooth, hairline-free text best.
